origins.section: The Step-03 Plan Claims Value Its Starts Don't Have
A Coefficient per Variable Prices Each Start Year
Maximizing NPV and Maximizing Risk Give Different Plans

gates.says: all 3 of this quiz's answerable readings held and each was taken over the question as it stands

recorded.prompt:q-flat-value: Read the whole lesson page, then this question. Using only what the page states, which option does the page decide is correct? Quote or cite the deciding passage.
recorded.outcome:q-flat-value: Finance: you value every project at its earliest-start NPV, whatever year you start it.
recorded.prompt:q-risk-years: Read the whole lesson page, then this question. Using only what the page states, which option does the page decide is correct? Quote or cite the deciding passage.
recorded.outcome:q-risk-years: A start in $t$ finishes the work at the end of year $t + d_i - 1$, so it removes the risk of every year from $t + d_i$ to the plan's last year (lesson 7.3.4).
recorded.prompt:q-report-both: Read the whole lesson page, then this question. Using only what the page states, which option does the page decide is correct? Quote or cite the deciding passage.
recorded.outcome:q-report-both: Whatever is maximized, the plan's NPV and risk are both reported.

recorded.prompt:q-flat-value:a: Using only what the lesson page states, does a passage of the page rule this option out? Cite the passage, or say none does or that the option is partly true. Be strict.
recorded.outcome:q-flat-value:a: Finance: you value every project at its earliest-start NPV, whatever year you start it.
